results.reason: Part 1 says the 10-Business-Day window under §5.7(b) for the September 14 First Schedule Supplement expired, citing the October 13 letter. It explains that under §5.7(c) the Ferrovane non-renewal is deemed cured for Article IX indemnity and the §7.2(a) bring-down, so the walk right and the indemnity are lost.

Part 3 identifies the Escrow Agreement's narrow out-of-pocket definition of Losses, which excludes diminution in value, lost profits, consequential damages and attorneys' fees. It explains that the §11.11 carve-out for disbursement mechanics makes this narrower definition limit escrow recovery.

Part 2 identifies the MSA §14.2 trigger at more than 50% of voting equity, which the 100% share sale meets. It notes the consent is absent from Annex 7.2(d) and so is not a §7.2(d) condition, and that the §4.4 representation is inaccurate. It explains that Buyer could be obligated to close and then face termination or List Price repricing by its sole-source supplier.
The memo states the window closed on Monday, September 28, 2026, more than two weeks before the October 13 letter.
The memo states the escrow amount as $4,850,000 more than once.

The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has a 'Where it appears' section with document and section citations, a 'Why it matters for Harrowgate' section and a 'Recommended fix' section.
Section 6 is a table of open points that cannot be resolved from the documents, with the source of input for each, including the client.
The memo expressly states that Harrowgate no longer has a termination right for the Ferrovane matter.
The memo states that Tavinor is not listed in Annex 7.2(d) and that its consent is not a closing condition.
